patch.description: Tesla opened its dedicated Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada on September 24, 2026. Opening coverage gives 1.8 million square feet and a design target of 50,000 trucks annually, rather than verified achieved output.
patch.longFormSummary:
• Tesla announced on 24 August 2026, via a post from the @tesla_semi account reading "Inauguration of new Semi factory in Nevada next month," that it would inaugurate its new Semi plant; the attached image was titled 'Semi Rollout' and carried the date September 24th 2026
  • The invite-only "Tesla Semi Rollout" takes place on Thursday, 24 September 2026 at the dedicated Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada, next door to Gigafactory Nevada, as the official celebration of the plant's opening
  • Attendees get guided factory tours of the newly commissioned high-volume assembly lines plus ride-alongs in the updated production Semi, with food and refreshments served
  • The guest list is aimed at fleet customers, employees and a small number of creators; each confirmed invitee may bring one additional guest, RSVPs were due before midnight Pacific Time on Wednesday, 2 September 2026, and confirmed attendees receive a follow-up email with next steps
  • Entry rules mirror the Cybercab event: IDs checked on arrival, no one under 21 admitted, and Tesla reserves the right to deny entry
  • Tesla began emailing invitations by 11 September 2026 — teardown expert Sandy Munro (@live_munro) shared his, showing a frontal view of the refreshed Semi framed by illuminated tunnel arches — after Sawyer Merritt first posted an official invite on 24 August
  • Tesla has not confirmed a livestream; commentators note last week's Cybercab launch in Austin was not broadcast and that a Class 8 fleet-focused truck may warrant a closed-door industry gathering, in which case first photos and ride notes would come from guests
  • The event is ceremonial rather than a production start: the first Semi rolled off the high-volume line on 29 April 2026 (announced via X by programme director Dan Priestley), roughly five months before the inauguration, and Tesla has been delivering to customers under test programmes for months
  • Expected programme topics include production innovations, fleet economics and total cost of ownership versus diesel, autonomy roadmaps after Tesla confirmed Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is coming to the Semi, and expanded global availability
  • It follows Tesla's European push at IAA Transportation in Hannover (15–20 September 2026), where Tesla gave the European spec — 550 km at 40 tonnes, 800 kW Megacharging, 9,100 kg curb weight — with customer demos in the first half of 2027 and deliveries targeted by the end of that year, all built in Nevada; Priestley said a European factory is "not on the table yet"
  • The Rollout sits between Cybercab public rides, which began in Austin on 3 September, and the Roadster event on 1 October in Waco
  • Context on demand and charging: Einride's 500-truck order is the largest public Semi deal, with first units landing this month in California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois and Georgia; Pepsi and Frito-Lay have years on the pilot fleet; Tesla opened the world's first public Semi Megacharger site in July, and Canada's first MCS sites are planned in Langley and Kamloops for a 12-truck Plett order with 2027 deliveries
  • Analysts estimate 5,000–15,000 Semis delivered in 2026, far short of nameplate capacity, with 50,000 units/year described as "a ceiling, not a run rate"; Electrek expects Tesla to use the stage to reset 2026 delivery expectations

Notable features

  • The Sparks plant is a dedicated Semi factory of roughly 1.8 million square feet, engineered for up to 50,000 Class 8 electric trucks a year once fully ramped, built beside Gigafactory Nevada as part of a US$3.6 billion expansion announced in 2023, with hiring for the ramp starting in early 2025
  • Its key advantage is vertical integration — most manufacturing under one roof, with Semi output tied directly to 4680 cell production at the neighbouring site, which Tesla says insulates the programme from supply-chain disruption
  • The production Semi is substantially revised from the 2022 pilot truck delivered to PepsiCo: electric steering assist replacing hydraulics, upgraded actuators, a 48-volt electrical architecture, custom 4680 cells built for a million-mile commercial duty cycle, independent front suspension and a new front light bar
  • The 48V architecture and optimised battery housing cut about 450 kg from total vehicle weight
  • Two variants: Standard Range at about 325 miles (under 20,000 lb curb weight) and Long Range at about 500 miles (23,000 lb curb weight, 822 kWh pack), both rated at 82,000 lb maximum load
  • Powertrain: three independent motors on the rear axles with up to 800 kW output, more than 1,000 horsepower
  • Claimed efficiency of about 1.7 kWh per mile at 82,000 lb GCW — called the Semi's most defensible competitive claim
  • Charging via MCS 3.2 Megacharger at up to 1.2 MW, restoring roughly 60–70% of range in about 30 minutes; ePTO rated to 25 kW for trailer functions such as refrigeration
  • The truck carries 10 cameras and is designed for autonomy — Tesla has confirmed FSD is coming in a future update and production units have been spotted with FSD testing hardware on public roads
  • Competitive context: Volvo leads global e-truck shipments, Daimler's Freightliner eCascadia leads North American Class 8 EVs on a 230-mile range backed by thousands of service bays, BYD's 8TT targets charging speeds rivalling Megacharger, and startup Windrose undercuts Tesla at US$285,000 against the Semi's US$300,000 even with 70% import duties
  • Opening follow-up: the dedicated plant opened September 24, 2026. Tesla’s design target is 50,000 trucks a year, not demonstrated current annual throughput. Opening coverage reports 1.8 million square feet, superseding the pre-event 1.7 million figure.
  • No separate published budget for this Semi-only factory phase was verified. The previously announced combined Semi and battery investment is not used as this phase’s cost.

patch.description: October 28 evening Brent snapshot: largest adjacent midpoint band USD 110.99–112.99/barrel; 213,149.05 contracts. USD 106,572.85 is a derived turnover proxy, not reported cash volume.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: October 28 evening research snapshot: 30 active October Brent strikes. Largest adjacent midpoint-implied band USD 110.99–112.99/barrel (20.0 percentage-point drop). Nearest 50% threshold USD 110.99, Yes bid/ask 44–50%. Volume totals 213,149.05 contract units; contracts times last prices give USD 106,572.85, a derived turnover proxy, not reported cash volume. patch.longFormSummary:
• October 28 evening research snapshot: 30 active October Brent strikes. Largest adjacent midpoint-implied band USD 110.99–112.99/barrel (20.0 percentage-point drop). Nearest 50% threshold USD 110.99, Yes bid/ask 44–50%. Volume totals 213,149.05 contract units; contracts times last prices give USD 106,572.85, a derived turnover proxy, not reported cash volume. Sparse threshold quotes are not a precise probability density. October is still active and has no realized settlement; preserve October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC and the September parent.
  • October 28, 2026 morning observation (2026-10-28T13:49:24.070Z): 30 active October Brent strikes. The largest adjacent midpoint-implied band is USD 108.99–110.99/barrel (17.5 percentage-point drop). The USD 110.99 threshold is nearest 50%: Yes bid 49%, ask 52%, midpoint 50.5%. This is a noisy reading of cumulative threshold quotes, not a precise probability density.
  • Volume is 201,689.98 contract units. Summing each contract’s volume multiplied by its latest price gives USD 107,723.11, a derived turnover proxy, not exchange-reported cash volume. October remains active without a realized value. The observation stays October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC and the thread continues from September.
  • October 27, 2026 evening snapshot (2026-10-27T23:46:58.954117+00:00): 30 active October Brent strikes. Largest adjacent midpoint-implied band USD 106.99–108.99 per barrel (18.5 percentage-point drop). Nearest 50% threshold USD 108.99, midpoint 54.5%, bid 53%, ask 56%. Summed volume 200,178.60 contract units; contracts times latest prices imply USD 97,628.42 turnover proxy, not exchange-reported dollar volume. Sparse/non-monotonic quotes make adjacent bands noisy. October remains unsettled; preserve October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC and the September parent.
  • October 27, 2026 morning snapshot: 30 active October Brent strikes. Largest adjacent midpoint-implied band USD 108.99–110.99 per barrel (16.5 percentage-point drop). Nearest 50% threshold is USD 110.99: midpoint 43%, bid 41%, ask 45%; USD 108.99 has midpoint 59.5%. Summed volume 195,687.25 contract units; contracts times last prices imply USD 100,434.62 turnover proxy, not exchange-reported dollar volume. Non-monotonic sparse quotes make adjacent bands noisy. No realized October settlement: observation remains October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC.
  • October 26, 2026 morning snapshot: 30 active October strikes. The largest adjacent midpoint-probability drop is USD 110.99–112.99/barrel (15.0 percentage points); the threshold nearest 50% is USD 108.99, midpoint 54.0% (bid/ask 52–56%). Volume totals 188,942.21 contract units. Summing each contract’s volume times its last price implies USD 97,996.10, a derived turnover proxy, not exchange-reported cash volume. Sparse and non-monotonic quotes make the band noisy. All remain active with no realized settlement; observation remains October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC.
  • Evening observation, October25,2026 Pacific (October26 UTC): the30active October strikes have their largest adjacent midpoint-probability drop between US$106.99 and US$108.99 per barrel, about19 percentage points. The US$108.99 threshold is closest to50%: midpoint50.5%, Yes bid49¢/ask52¢. This is a noisy market-implied band, not a point estimate or a calibrated probability interval.
  • Volume basis:186,157.36 traded contract units across the October ladder. Summing units times each contract’s latest price yields approximatelyUS$97,064.46 estimated turnover. This is a derived snapshot proxy, not reported cash volume; changing last prices can make it fall even as contracts traded increase. It must not be compared as a cash-volume time series with earlier estimates.
  • The current operator rules say October’s settlement uses the Pyth Brent Crude Oil24/7 index, replacing the front-month futures methodology for settlements from September30. It uses the close of the one-minute candle ending October30 at5p.m. EDT (21:00UTC), rounded to two decimals. This is not a monthly average, WTI price or realized settlement. All October contracts remain active with no settlement value.
  • October 25, 2026 morning snapshot (2026-10-25T15:00:38.120078+00:00): 30 active October Brent strikes. The largest adjacent midpoint-implied band is US$114.99–116.99/bbl (13.0 percentage points), while the threshold nearest50% is US$110.99 at 49.5% (bid/ask 48–51%). Summed contracts times last prices imply estimated dollar turnover US$101,823.38; this is not reported cash volume. Non-monotonic tails make adjacent differences noisy, not a precise density. Observation remains October30 at17:00EDT/21:00UTC and is not yet settled.
  • October24,2026 morning (snapshot checked 2026-10-24T14:08:19.135977+00:00): 30 October Brent strikes. Leading adjacent midpoint-implied band US$108.99–110.99/bbl (16.0 percentage points); closest50%threshold US$110.99 at 49.5%. Contracts times last prices imply estimated dollar turnover US$99,499.22, not reported cash volume. Non-monotonic thresholds make these differences noisy rather than a precise probability density. Observation remains October30 at17:00EDT/21:00UTC; October is not settled.
  • October23,2026 evening (snapshot checked 2026-10-24T03:54:04.988370+00:00): 30 October Brent strikes. Leading adjacent midpoint-implied band US$108.99–110.99/bbl (10.5 percentage points); closest50%threshold US$110.99 at 50%. Contracts times last prices imply estimated dollar turnover US$97,930.48, not reported cash volume. Non-monotonic thresholds make these differences noisy rather than a precise probability density. Observation remains October30 at17:00EDT/21:00UTC; October is not settled.
  • Observed October 23, 2026: the 30-strike October Brent book’s largest adjacent midpoint-implied band is US$108.99–110.99/bbl (12 percentage points). The closest midpoint to 50% is the US$108.99 threshold at 53%; its quoted bid/ask is 51–55%. Summed contracts times last-trade prices imply estimated dollar turnover of US$88,276.95, not exchange-reported cash volume. Non-monotonic thresholds make these differences a noisy distribution rather than a precise density. October remains unsettled; the observation is October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC.
  • On October 22, 2026 at approximately 23:32 UTC, the raw Kalshi book contained 30 October Brent strikes. The largest adjacent midpoint-implied band was US$106.99–108.99/bbl (17 percentage points); nearest 50% threshold US$108.99. Contracts times last prices total an estimated US$83,954.71, not reported cash turnover. Non-monotonic outliers mean these adjacent differences are not a precise probability density. Observation remains October 30, 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC. The month has not settled.
  • October 21,2026 PM book: 30 October Brent strikes; the largest adjacent midpoint-implied band was US$106.99–108.99/bbl (16.5 percentage points), with nearest 50%threshold US$106.99. Contract count times last price totals an estimated US$71,805.77, not reported cash turnover. Outlying thresholds remain non-monotonic, so these differences are not a precise probability density. Observation remains October 30 at 17:00 EDT/21:00 UTC; the October contract is unsettled.
  • On October 20, 2026 the 30-strike October Brent book’s largest adjacent midpoint-implied band was US$106.99–108.99/bbl (21.5 percentage points). The nearest 50% threshold was US$104.99. Summed contracts times last price was an estimated US$72,901.59, not exchange-reported dollar turnover. Some outlying thresholds are non-monotonic and the distribution is not a precise probability density. The observation remains October 30 at 17:00 EDT / 21:00 UTC; October has not settled.
  • This monthly Brent forecast resolves to the contract-defined one-minute closing price on October 30, 2026 at 17:00 EDT (21:00 UTC). It is neither the monthly average spot price nor a physical cargo purchase. Kalshi’s rules, rather than a later administrative settlement buffer, determine the timestamp.
  • Observed October 16, the 30-strike book quoted 71–75% bid/ask above US$100.99/bbl, 54–55% above US$102.99, and 44–45% above US$104.99. Midpoint differences between adjacent cumulative thresholds put the largest quoted band around US$101–103; the 50% crossing is nearer US$104. These derived readings are not a guaranteed final value.
  • Dollar turnover is estimated at US$59,668 by summing each strike’s traded-contract count multiplied by its last-trade dollar price. Kalshi contract counts are not dollar volume. This estimate can differ from exchange-displayed turnover, and last prices can lag the bid/ask quotes used above. No turnover amount is entered as the event’s cost.
  • EIA’s October outlook forecasts a US$105/bbl average Brent spot price for Q 4, against constrained Middle East flows, inventory withdrawals and tight diesel markets. It assumes flows improve over time and expects US$84 for the 2027 annual average. These provide independent market context; quarterly spot averages and this single contract observation are different benchmarks.
  • The forecast will be checked against the finalized contract value. A later outcome review must compare that value with this preserved October 16 distribution and contemporaneous inventory, shipping, supply and demand evidence. The October 16 forecast is preserved here; separate historical monthly records were subsequently linked in this thread.
  • On October 17, 2026, the October 30 book quoted 56–60% bid/ask aboveUS$104.99,48–51% aboveUS$106.99 and 40–43% aboveUS$108.99 per barrel. The median threshold moved towardUS$107. The largest adjacent midpoint-probability difference was aroundUS$111–113, approximately 10.5 percentage points; this derived modal band is sensitive to sparse quotes and is not a point forecast.
  • Across 30 strikes, approximately 129,355.46 traded contracts imply an estimatedUS$66,049 when each count is multiplied by its last-trade price. This is an estimate of dollar turnover, not exchange-reported exact dollars or oil-purchase cost. Earlier October 16 odds remain above for comparison. The event remains the October 30, 17:00 EDT observation; this October observation has not yet realized.
  • Across 30 current strikes the largest adjacent midpoint-implied band is US$98.99–100.99 (about 11.0 percentage points); the closest 50% threshold is US$106.99 at 47.0%. Estimated turnover is US$68,495, computed as contracts times last prices, not exact exchange-reported dollar volume. Earlier dated snapshots remain above. No realized October price is available; observation remains October 30,17:00 EDT.
  • On October 19, 2026, the 30-strike October 30 Brent book’s largest adjacent midpoint-implied band was US$106.99–108.99/bbl, about 14.5 percentage points. The closest 50% threshold was US$104.99. Summed contracts times each last price gives an estimated US$67,667, not exact exchange-reported dollar turnover. Last-price changes can lower this estimate even when cumulative contract volume rises. The event remains the October 30,17:00 EDT observation; no October realized settlement is available.

note: Refreshed dated October Brent distribution without forcing realization or changing settlement/parent.
